stem: Which combination represents the CDC hierarchy used in a tuberculosis infection-control program for healthcare settings?

options.A: Administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment.
options.B: Contact precautions, surgical hand antisepsis, and environmental surface disinfection.
options.C: Staff antibiotic prophylaxis, ultraviolet exposure, and elimination of symptom screening.
options.D: Standard Precautions alone, without a separate respiratory-protection component.

rationale: Current CDC guidance states that healthcare TB infection-control programs should use a three-level hierarchy: administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment. Administrative controls are the first and most important level; environmental controls reduce the concentration/spread of airborne TB bacteria; respiratory protection provides an additional layer in high-risk exposure situations. Therefore A is correct. The other options do not represent the CDC hierarchy.
educational_objective: Identify the CDC three-level hierarchy for healthcare TB infection control: administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment.

source_original.stem: Which combination represents the CDC hierarchy used in a tuberculosis infection-control program for healthcare settings?

options.A: Use a hierarchy of administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment for healthcare TB infection control.
options.B: Use contact precautions, surgical hand antisepsis, and environmental surface disinfection as the three levels of TB control.
options.C: Use staff antibiotic prophylaxis, ultraviolet exposure, and elimination of symptom screening as the three control levels.
options.D: Use standard precautions alone, because a separate respiratory-protection component is not part of healthcare TB control.

source_original.rationale: CDC describes a three-level hierarchy for healthcare TB infection control: administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment. Administrative measures are the first and most important level and include prompt recognition and management of people with suspected infectious TB.
source_original.source_detail: Three-level hierarchy: administrative measures, environmental controls, respiratory protective equipment Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the CDC TB-control hierarchy construct and key A, simplified all options into parallel control-framework statements, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct CDC hierarchy.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC TB healthcare guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Tuberculosis Infection Control > Summary of Guidelines and the three hierarchy sections
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the exact CDC three-level hierarchy and avoids substituting general PPE or unrelated infection-control measures for the specific TB framework.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; these are not the three CDC TB-control hierarchy levels.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; antibiotic prophylaxis/elimination of screening are not hierarchy components.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; respiratory protection is explicitly the third level of the hierarchy.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reproduces all three CDC hierarchy levels correctly.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are control-framework descriptions; the key depends on the official hierarchy rather than option length.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — airborne-disease prevention and respiratory-protection systems.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC TB infection-control page, all three hierarchy levels, all options, rationale, objective, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN category alignment. A remained uniquely correct.
